section: Elements and factors of climate; world climatic classification (Koeppen)
subsections: Controls of climate - factors and how each operates
Identifying a climate type from a description

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT regarded as a control of climate?
accepted.x: Distance from a river is not a recognised control of climate. Latitude, altitude and distance from the sea influence climatic conditions.
accepted.tq: Find the factor that does not belong to the standard climatic controls.
accepted.sec: Controls of climate - factors and how each operates

accepted.s: The mainland of India lies approximately between which latitudes?
accepted.x: India’s mainland extends approximately from 8°N to 37°N. Insolation generally decreases towards the poles.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise geographical range rather than the broader regional location.
accepted.sec: Controls of climate - factors and how each operates

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding latitude as a climatic control:
1. The angle of the Sun’s rays varies with latitude.
2. Insolation generally decreases poleward.
3. Areas south of the Tropic of Cancer in India are broadly tropical.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Latitude affects the angle of solar rays and the amount of insolation received.
accepted.tq: Test the linked effects of latitude through a coded combination.
accepted.sec: Controls of climate - factors and how each operates

accepted.s: The normal rate at which temperature decreases with increase in altitude is approximately
accepted.x: Temperature falls at approximately 6.5°C for every 1,000 metres of ascent under the normal lapse rate.
accepted.tq: Use the standard numerical value associated with altitude and temperature.
accepted.sec: Controls of climate - factors and how each operates

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): Coastal areas generally experience an equable climate.
Reason (R): The sea moderates temperature and reduces the intensity of seasonal extremes.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true, and the moderating influence of the sea explains why coastal areas have a maritime or equable climate.
accepted.tq: Check whether the stated physical process directly explains the climatic effect.
accepted.sec: Controls of climate - factors and how each operates

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the climatic contrast produced by distance from the sea?
o: Distance from the sea affects rainfall but not temperature
Coastal areas have continental extremes, while interiors are equable
Coastal areas are generally equable, while interiors experience greater extremes
Both coasts and interiors have identical seasonal ranges
accepted.x: The sea moderates temperatures near the coast, whereas inland areas tend to experience greater temperature extremes and a continental climate.
accepted.tq: Identify the correctly reversed coastal–continental comparison.
accepted.sec: Controls of climate - factors and how each operates

accepted.s: The primary climatic role of the Himalayas in northern India is to
o: allow cold Central Asian winds to enter freely
prevent all rainfall over northern India
block cold Central Asian winds and help trap the monsoon
produce a permanent high-pressure belt over the Deccan
accepted.x: The Himalayas block cold Central Asian winds and help retain the monsoon winds, thereby influencing the climate of northern India.
accepted.tq: Match the mountain barrier with its specific climatic function.
accepted.sec: Controls of climate - factors and how each operates

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about relief and climate:
1. Windward slopes generally receive more rainfall.
2. Leeward slopes may lie in a rain-shadow region.
3. The Himalayas keep northern India about 3–8°C warmer in winter than places on the same latitude.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Relief causes windward rainfall and leeward rain-shadow conditions, while the Himalayas moderate winter temperatures in northern India.
accepted.tq: Combine the direct and comparative effects of relief in a coded option.
accepted.sec: Controls of climate - factors and how each operates

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding ocean currents and climate is correct?
o: Ocean currents have no effect on coastal climates
Warm currents make tropical western coasts permanently arid
Cold currents make tropical western coasts cool and dry
Cold currents make eastern continental coasts warm and rainy
accepted.x: Cold currents cool and dry adjacent coasts, particularly on the western margins of tropical continents. Warm currents tend to make coasts warmer and wetter.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the contrasting effects of cold and warm currents.
accepted.sec: Controls of climate - factors and how each operates

accepted.s: Warm ocean currents generally make the adjoining east coasts of continents
o: dry because of offshore trade winds
accepted.x: Warm currents raise coastal temperatures and contribute to wetter conditions on adjoining east coasts.
accepted.tq: Recall the coast–current relationship without reversing warm and cold effects.
accepted.sec: Controls of climate - factors and how each operates

accepted.s: Which of the following is a set of climatic influences associated with winds and pressure belts?
o: Monsoons, westerlies, western disturbances and cyclones
Tides, ocean trenches, glaciers and earthquakes
River capture, folding, faulting and weathering
Volcanoes, soil horizons, deltas and plateaus
accepted.x: Monsoons, westerlies, western disturbances and cyclones are atmospheric circulation features associated with winds and pressure systems.
accepted.tq: Select the group belonging to atmospheric circulation rather than geomorphic processes.
accepted.sec: Controls of climate - factors and how each operates

accepted.s: The lowest temperature ever recorded on Earth is associated with
accepted.x: Vostok in Antarctica recorded the lowest known temperature, about −89.2°C. Oymyakon and Verkhoyansk are associated with the cold pole among inhabited places.
accepted.tq: Separate the absolute recorded extreme from the coldest inhabited locations.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the exceptional rainfall of Mawsynram and Cherrapunji?
o: Funnelling of moist air and orographic lifting
Cold currents and subtropical high pressure
accepted.x: Mawsynram and Cherrapunji receive more than 1,100 cm of annual rainfall because moist air is funnelled and forced to rise over the terrain.
accepted.tq: Link the climatic extreme to the physical mechanism producing it.

accepted.s: Mawsynram, located in the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, receives a mean annual rainfall of approximately
accepted.x: Mawsynram has a mean annual rainfall of about 1,187 cm, making it one of the wettest places on Earth.
accepted.tq: Place the decimal scale correctly when interpreting an extreme rainfall figure.

accepted.s: The Atacama Desert is regarded as one of the driest regions of the world and is located in
o: central Australia, west of the Great Dividing Range
southern Argentina, east of the Andes
the interior of the Arabian Peninsula
northern Chile, west of the Andes
accepted.x: The Atacama Desert lies in northern Chile, west of the Andes, and is recognised for extreme aridity.
accepted.tq: Combine the climatic superlative with the correct location.

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Ganganagar — approximately 50°C in 1935
2. Dras — approximately −45°C in 1908
3. Ruyli, Jaisalmer — about 8.33 cm annual rainfall
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correct. Ganganagar represents India’s highest noted temperature, Dras its lowest noted temperature, and Ruyli its driest location in the cited records.
accepted.tq: Verify each numerical place–record pair before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s: Hot deserts are generally concentrated between approximately
accepted.x: Hot deserts commonly occur between 15° and 30° north and south, especially on the western margins of continents.
accepted.tq: Recall the latitudinal belt associated with subtropical hot deserts.

accepted.s: Which combination best explains the occurrence of hot deserts on the western margins of continents?
o: Subtropical high pressure, offshore trade winds and cold currents
Polar easterlies, glaciers and high humidity
Equatorial low pressure, onshore trade winds and warm currents
Monsoon depressions, warm currents and rising air
accepted.x: Subtropical high pressure suppresses rainfall, offshore trade winds reduce moisture supply, and cold currents further stabilise and dry the air.
accepted.tq: Match the desert location with the combined pressure, wind and current conditions.

accepted.s: The Bedouins are traditionally associated with which natural region and way of life?
o: Arabian and Saharan deserts and nomadism
Equatorial forests and hunting of forest animals
Central Asian steppes and settled cultivation
accepted.x: Bedouins are traditionally nomadic people of the hot deserts of Arabia and the Sahara.
accepted.tq: Match the people with both their natural region and characteristic livelihood.

accepted.s: The Kirghiz and Kazakh peoples are traditionally associated with the
accepted.x: The Kirghiz and Kazakh peoples are associated with the grasslands and steppes of Central Asia.
accepted.tq: Use the natural-region association to distinguish steppe peoples from desert and tundra groups.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Yakuts are associated with Siberia and the taiga or Arctic environment. The Tuareg are associated with the Sahara, while the Bedouin are associated with Arabia and the Sahara.
accepted.tq: Start from the complete three-part match and reject swapped environments.

accepted.s: The Tuareg people are primarily associated with the
o: Central Asian steppes and temperate grassland climate
accepted.x: The Tuareg are traditionally associated with the Sahara and its hot desert environment.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely placed desert and steppe associations.

accepted.s: Mediterranean climate receives most of its rainfall during winter because
o: the subtropical high-pressure belt dominates in winter
cold ocean currents produce continuous monsoon rainfall
westerly depressions and cyclonic systems affect the region in winter
the trade winds reverse and produce convection throughout winter
accepted.x: In winter, the seasonal shift of pressure belts allows westerly depressions to bring cyclonic rainfall to Mediterranean regions.
accepted.tq: Connect the seasonal pressure-belt shift with the timing of rainfall.

accepted.s: Which one of the following climatic descriptions is characteristic of the Mediterranean climate?
o: Severe winters and short, cool summers
Hot, wet summers and long, dry winters
Hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters
Rainfall throughout the year with negligible annual range
accepted.x: Mediterranean climate is characterised by hot, dry and sunny summers and mild, wet winters.
accepted.tq: Separate Mediterranean conditions from savanna and taiga descriptions.

accepted.s: Mediterranean climate is generally found between approximately
accepted.x: Mediterranean climate occurs mainly between 30° and 45° north and south, particularly on the western margins of continents.
accepted.tq: Recall both the latitude belt and the western-margin setting.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with Mediterranean climate?
accepted.x: Darwin is not among the listed Mediterranean climatic locations. Mediterranean conditions occur in places such as Santiago, Cape Town and Perth.
accepted.tq: Find the location outside the recognised Mediterranean-climate regions.

accepted.s: In India, the climatic type corresponding to Koeppen’s As classification is associated with the
accepted.x: Koeppen’s As climate, characterised by dry summers and winter rainfall, occurs on the Coromandel Coast of Tamil Nadu.
accepted.tq: Match the Koeppen symbol with its Indian regional occurrence.

accepted.s: The Mediterranean climatic region is popularly known for the cultivation of
accepted.x: Mediterranean regions are known as orchard lands and are associated with citrus fruits, grapes and wine production.
accepted.tq: Use the characteristic crop association to identify the climate.

accepted.s: A region has a very small annual temperature range of 2–3°C and receives rainfall in every month. Which climate does it most likely represent?
accepted.x: A very small annual temperature range and year-round rainfall are characteristic of the equatorial climate.
accepted.tq: Identify the climate from its strongest temperature-range and rainfall clues.
accepted.sec: Identifying a climate type from a description

accepted.s: A region experiences a hot, wet summer followed by a long dry winter. This description most closely corresponds to
accepted.x: Hot wet summers and long dry winters are characteristic of savanna or monsoon climatic conditions.
accepted.tq: Distinguish summer-rain climates from the winter-rain Mediterranean type.
accepted.sec: Identifying a climate type from a description

accepted.s: A climate with very high temperatures, a very large daily range and annual rainfall below 25 cm is characteristic of
accepted.x: Extreme heat, a large diurnal temperature range and rainfall below 25 cm indicate a hot desert climate.
accepted.tq: Combine rainfall amount with daily temperature range to identify the desert type.
accepted.sec: Identifying a climate type from a description

accepted.s: Which climatic description correctly represents the taiga climate of Siberia?
o: Warm dry summer and mild wet winter
Long severe winter, short cool summer and very large annual range
Warmest month below 10°C with no seasonal contrast
Very small annual temperature range and rainfall every month
accepted.x: The taiga climate has a long severe winter, a short cool summer and a very large annual temperature range.
accepted.tq: Select the description containing the decisive seasonal-range features of taiga.
accepted.sec: Identifying a climate type from a description

accepted.s: A place where the warmest month has a temperature below 10°C is generally classified as having
accepted.x: A warmest-month temperature below 10°C is a defining descriptive feature of the tundra climate.
accepted.tq: Use the temperature threshold as the decisive classification clue.
accepted.sec: Identifying a climate type from a description
